Note::NlpAccessor::remove_urls¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::remove_urls() const

Delete Web URLs From Each Cell¶

remove_urls() removes web links from every text cell and tidies the whitespace left behind. Use it as a text-preprocessing step when links are noise for the downstream task — building a bag-of-words model, computing readability, de-duplicating near-identical messages, or preparing prompt context where the URL adds tokens but no signal.

A span is treated as a URL when it starts with http://, https://, or www. (case-insensitive) and runs until the next whitespace or one of <, >, ", ', ), ]. That covers the common cases — schemes and www. hosts with paths and query strings — but deliberately not bare domains without a scheme or www. prefix (example.com on its own is left alone), and not email addresses (use mask_pii for those).

After the links are cut, the surrounding whitespace is collapsed to single spaces and the cell is trimmed at both ends, so removing a URL from the middle of a sentence does not leave a double space or a dangling gap.

Contrast mask_pii, whose [URL] category replaces each link with a placeholder rather than deleting it: use mask_pii when the fact that a link was there matters, and remove_urls when it does not. The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note; a cell with no link is copied through unchanged.

Example 1: Links In The Middle Of Prose¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note(
        {"see https://pluss.dev/docs and www.example.com now", "no link here"})
        .nlp().remove_urls())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["see and now", "no link here"]

Both the https:// link and the www. host are removed, and the resulting run of spaces is collapsed. The second cell has no link and is unchanged.

Example 2: A Scalar With A Query String¶

const pluss::Note n =
    pluss::make_note("visit http://a.b/c?q=1 today").nlp().remove_urls();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"visit today"

The path and query string are part of the URL span and go with it.

Example 3: Non-URL Text Is Left Alone¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({"emails a@b.io are kept"}).nlp().remove_urls())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["emails a@b.io are kept"]

An email address has no http/www. prefix, so remove_urls does not touch it.

See Also¶

  • Note::NlpAccessor::mask_pii: replace URLs (and other identifying spans) with named placeholders instead of deleting them.

  • Note::remove_all: delete a known literal substring.

  • Note::RegexAccessor::findall: pull the URLs out for inspection or an allow-list.
